findings.message: Rule-bearing legacy code in Claims.Rules.depreciationRate matches no observation and has rule-bearing constructs without accepted authority (ast analyzer). No accepted authority: exemption shape 'if' on "Electronics" (line 17): no cited record and no accepted exception record names "Electronics"; exemption shape 'if' on "Furniture" (line 18): no cited record and no accepted exception record names "Furniture"; exemption shape 'if' on "Clothing" (line 19): no cited record and no accepted exception record names "Clothing"; numeric literal 0 (line 20): value 0 equals no declared parameter of an accepted or superseded record. Supported (matching rule): category test '= "Electronics"' (line 17): (b) parameter, "Electronics" is named by accepted DEC-CL12; numeric literal 0.18 (line 17): (b) parameter, value 0.18 = DEC-CL12.depreciation.Electronics (accepted, same form); category test '= "Furniture"' (line 18): (b) parameter, "Furniture" is named by accepted DEC-CL12; numeric literal 0.07 (line 18): (b) parameter, value 0.07 = DEC-CL12.depreciation.Furniture (accepted, same form); category test '= "Clothing"' (line 19): (b) parameter, "Clothing" is named by accepted DEC-CL12; numeric literal 0.22 (line 19): (b) parameter, value 0.22 = DEC-CL12.depreciation.Clothing (accepted, same form). A category exemption sits inside the symbol that carries accepted DEC-CL12: an exemption from DEC-CL12 needs its own decision record, whatever the code comments call it. Question for Actuarial: which accepted record, if any, authorizes it? New work must not reuse it until answered; the legacy code is left unchanged.
